svg.title: The default is to absorb the surprise
svg.desc: A whiteboard sketch showing three upstream schema changes and dlt's default handling of each - a new currency field becoming a column with nulls backfilled, a quoted string amount silently coerced to a double, and a removed field leaving the column with a null - then a four-position schema contract knob where evolve adds the column and loads the row, freeze raises a DataValidationError and loads nothing, discard_value loads the row without the column and discard_row makes the row vanish silently, with discard_row ringed in red; a nested JSON blob normalized into an orders table and an orders__items child table joined by generated id columns; and the actual freeze error message.
svg.text: The default is to absorb the surprise
three things upstream can do to you, and what dlt does by default
the row is GONE. No error, no count, no log.
the DEFAULT is evolve. That is a choice someone
else made for you - and it is usually the right
one, right up until it is not.
and what it does to a nested array
one array = one child table, automatically
Contract on columns with mode freeze is violated. Trying
to add column loyalty_tier to table orders but columns
freeze is not "safe" - it is a decision to stop
the pipeline rather than absorb a surprise. That
is a judgement call, not a default.
...so which mode does YOUR table want?
